title: AQuIRE: Awesome Quantum Information Research Explorer

taxonomy.name: Foundations and mathematical tools
taxonomy.description: The language of quantum information connects linear algebra, probability, physical states, and measurements. These resources build the prerequisites needed to read algorithm and hardware papers.

topics.name: Linear algebra and Hilbert spaces
topics.description: Hilbert spaces provide the state space for quantum systems; tensor products describe composition. Linear algebra is also the implementation language of gates and many simulators.

topics.name: Quantum states and density operators
topics.description: Density operators represent both pure states and statistical mixtures. Reduced states are essential when only part of a larger system is measured or controlled.

topics.name: Quantum measurements
topics.description: Measurements convert quantum states into classical outcomes according to a specified measurement model. General measurements require POVMs and instruments rather than only orthogonal projectors.

topics.name: Quantum channels and open systems
topics.description: Quantum channels describe physical transformations including noise and discarded subsystems. Open system models connect microscopic dynamics to experimentally observed decoherence.

topics.name: Quantum entropy and information measures
topics.description: Information measures quantify uncertainty, correlations, and distinguishability. Operational meanings depend on the coding, estimation, or security task being studied.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Linear algebra, probability, and introductory quantum mechanics
taxonomy.assessment: State normalization, operator properties, measurement definitions, and physical interpretation

taxonomy.name: Entanglement and quantum resources
taxonomy.description: Entanglement and other nonclassical resources supply capabilities that must be characterized separately from hardware size. Resource theory studies what operations can generate or consume each resource.

topics.name: Entanglement detection and quantification
topics.description: Entanglement criteria test whether a state is separable, while monotones quantify particular resources. Different measures need not order mixed states in the same way.

topics.name: Bell nonlocality and contextuality
topics.description: Bell nonlocality concerns correlations incompatible with local hidden variable models. Contextuality concerns dependence on measurement context and requires its own experimental assumptions.

topics.name: Coherence and resource theories
topics.description: Resource theories specify free states and operations before defining a resource. Coherence, asymmetry, and entanglement are related but distinct examples.

topics.name: Magic and stabilizer resources
topics.description: Magic characterizes resources outside stabilizer computation. It matters both for non Clifford computation and for the cost of classical simulation.

topics.name: Entanglement distillation
topics.description: Distillation converts noisy shared resources into fewer high quality ones. Rates and achievable fidelities depend on allowed communication and operation classes.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Density operators, composite systems, and basic information measures
taxonomy.assessment: Allowed operations, resource monotones, witness validity, and operational task

taxonomy.name: Models of quantum computation
taxonomy.description: Different models specify the available operations and how an algorithm is executed. Equivalence of models does not imply identical engineering costs or noise tolerance.

topics.name: Circuit and universal gate models
topics.description: A circuit is an ordered composition of gates and measurements. Universality describes what transformations can be approximated, while compilation determines their actual cost.

topics.name: Measurement based computing
topics.description: Measurement based computation processes an entangled resource state through adaptive local measurements. Classical feed forward and resource generation are part of the computation.

topics.name: Adiabatic quantum computing
topics.description: Adiabatic computation evolves a Hamiltonian along a path whose low energy states encode the answer. Gap behavior and schedule assumptions determine the required runtime.

topics.name: Quantum annealing
topics.description: Annealing seeks low energy solutions of an encoded optimization problem. Embedding, temperature, open system dynamics, and solution sampling distinguish hardware annealers from ideal adiabatic algorithms.

topics.name: Continuous variable computing
topics.description: Continuous variable systems encode information in modes with continuous quadratures. Universal computation generally needs suitable non Gaussian resources as well as Gaussian control.

topics.name: Topological computation and anyons
topics.description: Topological schemes encode and manipulate information using anyonic degrees of freedom. Mathematical universality and experimental identification of the required excitations are separate questions.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Qubits, unitary operations, and measurement
taxonomy.assessment: Model assumptions, universality, resource generation, and noise constraints

taxonomy.name: Quantum complexity and limitations
taxonomy.description: Complexity theory identifies conditional speedups and lower bounds. It also explains why a problem being quantum does not automatically make it efficiently solvable.

topics.name: Quantum complexity classes
topics.description: Complexity classes formalize efficiently solvable and verifiable quantum problems. A class inclusion or separation should be read together with its error and oracle model.

topics.name: Query complexity and lower bounds
topics.description: Query complexity counts accesses to an input oracle. This isolates useful theoretical questions but does not include the physical cost of constructing that oracle.

topics.name: Quantum communication complexity
topics.description: Communication complexity asks how much information must be exchanged to solve a distributed task. Prior entanglement and classical side channels change the model.

topics.name: Quantum advantage and sampling hardness
topics.description: Sampling advantage compares specified quantum distributions with classical algorithms under stated assumptions. A sampling demonstration is not by itself evidence of useful application advantage.

topics.name: Dequantization and classical limitations
topics.description: Dequantization identifies classical algorithms that reproduce a claimed benefit under comparable access assumptions. Input preparation and low rank structure often determine the comparison.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Algorithms, asymptotic analysis, and discrete mathematics
taxonomy.assessment: Oracle model, complexity assumptions, lower bounds, and input access

taxonomy.name: Core quantum algorithms
taxonomy.description: Primitive algorithms form reusable components of larger workflows. Their complexity must include data preparation, oracle construction, accuracy, and measurement costs.

topics.name: Quantum Fourier transform
topics.description: The quantum Fourier transform changes between computational and Fourier bases. It is a primitive in phase estimation and order finding rather than a general replacement for classical FFT output.

topics.name: Phase estimation
topics.description: Phase estimation extracts eigenphase information from controlled dynamics. Precision, coherent evolution time, and state overlap control its cost and success probability.

topics.name: Amplitude amplification and search
topics.description: Amplitude amplification raises the probability of a marked outcome. Search speedups are measured in oracle queries and must include the implementation of the marking operation.

topics.name: Amplitude estimation
topics.description: Amplitude estimation estimates a probability or expectation using structured quantum access. Near term variants trade coherent depth for sampling and inference.

topics.name: Quantum walks
topics.description: Quantum walks use interference in graph or configuration space to design algorithms. Walk dynamics, graph access, and hitting or detection tasks need separate definitions.

topics.name: Hidden subgroup and factoring algorithms
topics.description: Order finding underlies Shor factoring and discrete logarithm algorithms. Hidden subgroup methods generalize the structure, but non abelian cases have additional obstacles.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Quantum circuits, probability, and eigenvalue problems
taxonomy.assessment: Oracle construction, precision, state overlap, and output readout

taxonomy.name: Advanced algorithm design
taxonomy.description: Modern algorithm frameworks organize linear algebra, simulation, and optimization around carefully controlled access models. Resource estimates depend strongly on how operators are encoded.

topics.name: Block encoding and qubitization
topics.description: Block encodings embed an operator into a larger unitary, and qubitization builds controlled spectral transformations. Normalization and oracle construction are central resource assumptions.

topics.name: Quantum signal processing
topics.description: Quantum signal processing implements constrained polynomial transformations through phase sequences. Polynomial degree, phase synthesis, and approximation error determine algorithm costs.

topics.name: Quantum singular value transformation
topics.description: Singular value transformation applies polynomial functions to the singular values of a block encoded matrix. It unifies many algorithms while making access assumptions explicit.

topics.name: Linear combination of unitaries
topics.description: Linear combinations of unitaries implement operators using coherent selection and state preparation. Success probability and amplification overhead affect the final resource estimate.

topics.name: Quantum linear systems
topics.description: Quantum linear systems algorithms prepare a state related to a linear system solution. Extracting every solution component can remove the intended advantage.

topics.name: Quantum differential equations
topics.description: Differential equation algorithms encode time evolution or discretized solution vectors. Stability, conditioning, boundary conditions, and output observables all enter the analysis.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Linear algebra, core quantum algorithms, and approximation theory
taxonomy.assessment: Block encoding normalization, conditioning, polynomial degree, and total cost

taxonomy.name: Hamiltonian simulation and many body physics
taxonomy.description: Quantum simulation targets the evolution and observables of physical systems. Digital, analog, and hybrid approaches have different error budgets and verification methods.

topics.name: Digital Hamiltonian simulation
topics.description: Digital simulation approximates Hamiltonian evolution with a programmable sequence of gates. The comparison should include accuracy, sparsity, simulation time, and compilation cost.

topics.name: Analog quantum simulation
topics.description: Analog simulators engineer a physical Hamiltonian to approximate a target model. Calibration and validation are especially important when universal digital corrections are unavailable.

topics.name: Quantum lattice and spin models
topics.description: Lattice and spin models provide structured many body targets. Geometry, interactions, symmetry, and observable selection specify the actual simulation problem.

topics.name: Quantum thermal states
topics.description: Thermal state algorithms prepare or characterize Gibbs states and finite temperature observables. Mixing, equilibration, and energy normalization can dominate costs.

topics.name: Quantum dynamics and scrambling
topics.query: quantum scrambling out of time order
topics.description: Scrambling and transport characterize how information and operators spread through a system. Measured correlators need interpretation that accounts for noise and finite size.

topics.name: Lattice gauge theory simulation
topics.description: Gauge simulation encodes fields subject to local constraints. Truncation and gauge violation must be assessed along with gate noise and observable accuracy.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Quantum mechanics, Hamiltonians, and many body physics
taxonomy.assessment: Simulation error, model truncation, observables, and classical verification

taxonomy.name: Quantum chemistry and materials
taxonomy.description: Electronic structure is a major application area because quantum states can encode correlated wavefunctions. Practical workflows require molecular mappings, controlled errors, and meaningful classical comparisons.

topics.name: Electronic structure algorithms
topics.description: Electronic structure algorithms estimate properties of interacting electrons in selected basis sets. The physical accuracy target and active space define the application.

topics.name: Fermion to qubit mappings
topics.query: quantum Jordan Wigner Bravyi Kitaev mapping
topics.description: Fermion mappings translate anticommutation relations into qubit operators. Operator locality, symmetry reduction, and measurement cost depend on the mapping.

topics.name: Excited states and spectroscopy
topics.description: Excited state and response algorithms target spectra beyond the ground state. State preparation and transition observable estimation are separate resource demands.

topics.name: Quantum chemistry resource estimates
topics.description: Chemistry estimates translate an algorithm into logical and physical resources for a chosen accuracy. Molecular basis, code assumptions, and factory architecture should be stated.

topics.name: Quantum materials and condensed matter
topics.description: Materials applications study strongly correlated phases and properties. A proposed workflow should identify observables that inform a materials decision and compare against suitable classical methods.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Electronic structure, second quantization, and quantum algorithms
taxonomy.assessment: Basis set, active space, energy accuracy, mapping, and measured observables

taxonomy.name: Variational and hybrid quantum methods
taxonomy.description: Variational algorithms optimize a parameterized circuit with a classical loop. Trainability, sampling, noise, and optimizer costs must be evaluated along with the objective value.

topics.name: Variational quantum eigensolvers
topics.description: VQE minimizes measured energy with a parameterized circuit and classical optimization. Ansatz bias, shot noise, and optimizer convergence all affect the result.

topics.name: Quantum approximate optimization
topics.description: QAOA alternates cost evolution with a mixing operation to search for good solutions. Depth, constraints, parameter selection, and classical baseline quality determine the assessment.

topics.name: Ansatz design and expressibility
topics.description: An ansatz defines the states reachable during optimization. Expressibility alone is not a guarantee of trainability or low resource cost.

topics.name: Barren plateaus and trainability
topics.description: Barren plateau analyses study exponentially small or concentrated gradients. The conclusion depends on circuit ensembles, cost locality, initialization, and noise.

topics.name: Quantum gradients and optimization
topics.description: Gradient rules and optimization methods control the classical loop around a quantum circuit. Measurement complexity and gradient variance must accompany iteration counts.

topics.name: Quantum imaginary time evolution
topics.description: Imaginary time methods project toward low energy states through nonunitary evolution or approximations. Normalization and locality assumptions determine what is implementable.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Optimization, parameterized circuits, and measurement statistics
taxonomy.assessment: Ansatz bias, trainability, shot cost, noise, and optimizer convergence

taxonomy.name: Quantum machine learning
taxonomy.description: Quantum machine learning includes learning with quantum circuits and learning about quantum systems. Input encoding, sample complexity, classical comparisons, and trainability determine whether a method is useful.

topics.name: Quantum data encoding
topics.description: Data encodings specify how classical or quantum inputs enter a circuit. State preparation cost and repeated access must be included in learning complexity.

topics.name: Quantum kernels
topics.description: Quantum kernels estimate similarities using quantum feature maps. Expressive features can still yield concentrated kernels or costly training measurements.

topics.name: Quantum neural networks and classifiers
topics.description: Quantum neural networks use trainable quantum circuits as learning models. Their evaluation requires held out data, noise analysis, and comparable classical baselines.

topics.name: Quantum generative models
topics.description: Generative quantum models represent or sample data distributions. Training objectives, sample quality, likelihood access, and the data source define the task.

topics.name: Quantum reinforcement learning
topics.description: Quantum reinforcement learning studies quantum resources in sequential decision tasks. Coherent access to an environment is a substantial assumption and is not always physically available.

topics.name: Quantum learning theory
topics.description: Quantum learning theory analyzes sample complexity and generalization under explicit learning models. Results differ for classical data, quantum examples, and unknown quantum states.

topics.name: Machine learning for quantum systems
topics.query: machine learning quantum control error decoding
topics.description: Machine learning can assist calibration, control, characterization, and decoding of quantum hardware. This direction can be useful without claiming a speedup from a quantum learning model.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Machine learning, statistics, and quantum circuits
taxonomy.assessment: Input encoding, sample complexity, generalization, and classical comparison

taxonomy.name: Optimization and operations research
taxonomy.description: Quantum optimization includes annealing, variational methods, and algorithms with provable guarantees. Application results should report feasible solutions and comparisons to strong classical solvers.

topics.name: Combinatorial optimization
topics.description: Combinatorial methods encode discrete decisions and constraints into quantum workflows. Feasibility, approximation quality, and problem size must be reported.

topics.name: Quantum semidefinite programming
topics.description: Quantum SDP solvers use structured access to matrices and constraints. Their advantage depends on sparsity, rank, input models, and the required output.

topics.name: Quantum scheduling and routing
topics.description: Routing and scheduling applications combine difficult constraints with discrete optimization. Penalties and embedding can create substantial overhead or infeasible solutions.

topics.name: Quantum portfolio and financial estimation
topics.description: Financial algorithms include estimation, pricing, and portfolio models. Model calibration, input access, error tolerances, and real computational costs determine relevance.

topics.name: Quantum optimization benchmarks
topics.description: Optimization benchmarking compares solution quality, runtime, and scaling against strong classical solvers. A quantum label or a favorable small instance is insufficient evidence of advantage.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Optimization, constraint modeling, and algorithm analysis
taxonomy.assessment: Feasibility, approximation quality, embedding overhead, and solver baselines

taxonomy.name: Superconducting qubit hardware
taxonomy.description: Superconducting circuits combine microwave control, cryogenics, fabrication, and readout. Device coherence and gate fidelity must be distinguished from logical error performance.

topics.name: Transmon and circuit QED
topics.description: Transmons reduce charge sensitivity through circuit design and couple to microwave resonators. Coherence, anharmonicity, coupling, and control tradeoffs shape performance.

topics.name: Flux and fluxonium qubits
topics.description: Flux based circuits use magnetic flux and specialized inductive elements to define qubit transitions. Sweet spots and device parameters affect both noise and control.

topics.name: Superconducting gates and couplers
topics.description: Couplers and entangling gates control interactions between superconducting qubits. Gate error, residual coupling, leakage, and spectator effects require joint calibration.

topics.name: Superconducting readout
topics.description: Dispersive readout infers a qubit state from a coupled resonator response. Measurement speed, fidelity, backaction, and multiplexing compete.

topics.name: Cryogenic circuits and packaging
topics.description: Cryogenic packaging delivers signals while removing heat and controlling electromagnetic environments. System scaling includes wiring, thermal budgets, and electronics placement.

topics.name: Superconducting fabrication and loss
topics.description: Fabrication and materials affect loss, disorder, yield, and device uniformity. A scalable process must control interfaces as well as individual junction properties.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Microwave circuits, cryogenics, and solid state physics
taxonomy.assessment: Coherence, leakage, crosstalk, fabrication variation, and system wiring

taxonomy.name: Trapped ion quantum computing
taxonomy.description: Ion processors use internal states coupled through collective motion. Scaling requires high quality gates, optical control, shuttling, and modular interconnects.

topics.name: Ion traps and architectures
topics.description: Ion trap architectures confine and address charged atoms used as qubits. Trap geometry, motional modes, and modular organization affect scaling.

topics.name: Ion entangling gates
topics.description: Entangling ion gates typically use shared motion or geometric phases. Mode crowding, heating, optical noise, and pulse design determine achievable fidelity.

topics.name: Ion transport and QCCD
topics.query: quantum charge coupled device ion shuttling
topics.description: QCCD architectures move ions between operation regions. Transport must preserve quantum information and manage motional excitation and cooling.

topics.name: Ion optical control and readout
topics.description: Laser control and fluorescence readout link ion states to optical hardware. Addressing errors, stability, collection efficiency, and crosstalk matter.

topics.name: Photonic links between ions
topics.description: Photonic links generate entanglement between distant ion modules. Heralding rates, photon collection, indistinguishability, and memory lifetime constrain execution.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Atomic physics, optics, and motional dynamics
taxonomy.assessment: Gate fidelity, mode management, optical stability, and transport cost

taxonomy.name: Neutral atom and Rydberg processors
taxonomy.description: Neutral atom arrays offer reconfigurable geometries and interactions controlled by optical fields. Coherent gates, atom loss, rearrangement, and measurement determine computational reliability.

topics.name: Optical tweezer arrays
topics.description: Optical tweezers create reconfigurable arrays of individual atoms. Loading and rearrangement establish the geometry used by later simulation or gate operations.

topics.name: Rydberg blockade gates
topics.description: Rydberg excitation enables strong interactions and blockade gates. Decay, motion, pulse control, and blockade imperfections determine gate error.

topics.name: Neutral atom analog simulation
topics.description: Neutral atom simulators realize programmable interacting spin systems. Interpretation depends on the realized Hamiltonian and measured observable rather than array size alone.

topics.name: Neutral atom error correction
topics.description: Neutral atom error correction combines logical encodings with atom transport and syndrome measurement. Atom loss and measurement backaction require platform aware analysis.

topics.name: Alkaline earth atomic qubits
topics.query: alkaline earth nuclear spin quantum computing
topics.description: Alkaline earth and related atoms offer nuclear spin and optical transition resources. Storage, control, readout, and metastable state lifetimes must be considered together.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Atomic physics, optical trapping, and interacting spin models
taxonomy.assessment: Atom loading, loss, gate error, geometry, and measurement backaction

taxonomy.name: Spin qubits and semiconductor platforms
taxonomy.description: Spin qubits connect quantum control to semiconductor materials and nanofabrication. Scaling involves disorder, charge noise, wiring, exchange coupling, and readout.

topics.name: Silicon spin qubits
topics.description: Silicon spin qubits combine quantum dot confinement with magnetic or electrical control. Valley structure, isotopic purity, and disorder are key device variables.

topics.name: Germanium hole qubits
topics.description: Germanium hole systems provide strong electric control through spin orbit coupling. Strain, confinement, charge noise, and interactions determine operation quality.

topics.name: Donor qubits
topics.description: Donor processors use localized electron and nuclear spins in semiconductors. Placement, hyperfine control, and readout interfaces affect scalability.

topics.name: Spin readout and exchange gates
topics.description: Exchange operations couple nearby spins, while spin to charge conversion enables readout. Control uniformity and charge noise connect gate and measurement performance.

topics.name: Spin shuttling and scalable arrays
topics.description: Shuttling and array control seek to connect spin qubits beyond immediate neighbors. Transport coherence and wiring complexity become system level constraints.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Semiconductor physics, spin dynamics, and nanofabrication
taxonomy.assessment: Disorder, charge noise, valley structure, readout, and array wiring

taxonomy.name: Photonic quantum computing
taxonomy.description: Photonic approaches encode information in optical modes and use interference, measurements, and sometimes nonlinear interactions. Loss and resource generation are central engineering constraints.

topics.name: Linear optical computation
topics.description: Linear optics uses interference, measurement, and ancillary photons for computation. Probabilistic operations require resource accounting and feed forward.

topics.name: Boson sampling
topics.description: Boson sampling samples distributions produced by indistinguishable particles passing through an optical network. Loss, distinguishability, and classical simulation affect hardness claims.

topics.name: Integrated quantum photonics
topics.description: Integrated photonics places optical components on chips. Loss, phase stability, fabrication variation, and coupling to sources and detectors determine usable performance.

topics.name: Single photon sources and detectors
topics.description: Photon sources and detectors supply and measure optical quantum resources. Efficiency, purity, timing, and indistinguishability directly influence system scale.

topics.name: Photonic cluster and fusion computing
topics.description: Fusion based schemes combine smaller entangled states into computational resources. Loss tolerance and resource factory overhead are central design questions.

topics.name: Squeezing and Gaussian optics
topics.description: Gaussian optics controls continuous variable modes with squeezing and linear transformations. Non Gaussian resources determine capabilities beyond Gaussian simulation.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Quantum optics, interference, and photodetection
taxonomy.assessment: Loss, indistinguishability, source rate, detector efficiency, and resource overhead

taxonomy.name: Other qubit platforms and transduction
taxonomy.description: Additional platforms offer different routes to coherence, control, and connectivity. Quantum transduction connects devices that operate at different physical frequencies.

topics.name: Diamond NV centers
topics.description: NV centers combine electronic and nuclear spins with optical interfaces in diamond. Their computing and sensing uses should be distinguished when reading application claims.

topics.name: Silicon carbide defects
topics.description: Silicon carbide hosts optically addressable defects compatible with semiconductor fabrication. Coherence and interface properties depend on defect species and material quality.

topics.name: Topological superconducting devices
topics.description: Majorana proposals seek protected operations using topological superconductivity. Device observations, zero mode interpretation, and demonstrated logical operations require separate evidence.

topics.name: Molecular and nuclear spin processors
topics.query: molecular nuclear magnetic resonance quantum computing
topics.description: Molecular and NMR approaches manipulate coupled spin registers. Ensemble demonstrations can teach control and algorithms while facing distinct scalability limits.

topics.name: Quantum transduction
topics.description: Transducers convert quantum information between physical frequencies or platforms. Conversion efficiency and added noise jointly determine whether a link is useful.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Solid state or molecular physics and quantum control
taxonomy.assessment: Platform specific evidence, scalability, conversion efficiency, and added noise

taxonomy.name: Control calibration and noise characterization
taxonomy.description: Control engineering links physical devices to reliable operations. A noise model should be measured and tested rather than assumed to describe all operating regimes.

topics.name: Optimal quantum control
topics.description: Optimal control searches for pulses that implement target transformations under constraints. Robustness to parameter errors and hardware bandwidth should be tested.

topics.name: Dynamical decoupling
topics.description: Dynamical decoupling suppresses selected environmental couplings through pulse sequences. Finite pulse errors and noise spectra limit its effectiveness.

topics.name: Quantum noise spectroscopy
topics.description: Noise spectroscopy infers environmental fluctuations from controlled quantum probes. The reconstruction depends on filter functions and assumptions about noise statistics.

topics.name: Leakage crosstalk and correlated errors
topics.query: quantum qubit leakage crosstalk correlated errors
topics.description: Leakage and correlated errors violate simple independent Pauli models. Detection, reset, and system context are essential for realistic reliability estimates.

topics.name: Automated quantum calibration
topics.description: Automated calibration estimates and updates control parameters from measurements. Drift, latency, identifiability, and calibration cost affect closed loop performance.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Control theory, stochastic processes, and experimental statistics
taxonomy.assessment: Model identification, robustness, drift, calibration effort, and correlated noise

taxonomy.name: Quantum error correction codes
taxonomy.description: Error correction encodes logical information into larger physical systems and extracts error syndromes without directly measuring the logical state. Code performance depends on the physical error model and decoder.

topics.name: Stabilizer and CSS codes
topics.query: quantum stabilizer CSS error correction codes
topics.description: Stabilizer and CSS constructions specify logical subspaces through commuting checks. Syndrome measurement must reveal error information without revealing the logical state.

topics.name: Surface and toric codes
topics.description: Surface and toric codes use structured local checks and topological logical operators. Thresholds depend on the noise and syndrome circuit model.

topics.name: Quantum LDPC codes
topics.description: Quantum LDPC codes aim for sparse checks and improved encoding efficiency. Required connectivity, measurement circuits, and decoding are important implementation constraints.

topics.name: Bosonic error correction
topics.query: bosonic quantum error correction cat GKP
topics.description: Bosonic codes encode a logical system into oscillator states. Photon loss, finite energy, state preparation, and syndrome extraction determine protection.

topics.name: Subsystem and color codes
topics.description: Subsystem and color codes offer alternative check and logical gate structures. Gauge choices and measurement schedules affect both error correction and computation.

topics.name: Erasure and biased noise codes
topics.query: quantum erasure biased noise error correction
topics.description: Tailored codes exploit information about erasures or noise bias. Their benefit can disappear if detection or bias assumptions fail.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Pauli operators, circuits, and coding theory
taxonomy.assessment: Code distance, check structure, physical noise, syndrome extraction, and decoding

taxonomy.name: Fault tolerance and logical operations
taxonomy.description: Fault tolerance ensures that errors during correction and computation do not spread uncontrollably. Logical gates and routing must be evaluated with the entire correction cycle.

topics.name: Thresholds and logical error scaling
topics.query: quantum fault tolerance threshold logical error
topics.description: Threshold analyses determine when larger encodings can suppress logical error. Finite distance performance and realistic correlations are needed for engineering decisions.

topics.name: Magic state distillation
topics.description: Magic state factories produce resources for non Clifford logical gates. Distillation yield, scheduling, and physical volume can dominate a large computation.

topics.name: Lattice surgery
topics.description: Lattice surgery implements logical parity operations through changing code boundaries. Routing and time steps must be included in algorithm mapping.

topics.name: Transversal gates and code switching
topics.description: Transversal gates and code switching manage logical operations while limiting error spread. Universality restrictions motivate combining multiple methods.

topics.name: Fault tolerant resource estimation
topics.description: Resource estimation turns logical circuits into physical hardware and runtime requirements. Error budgets, code distance, connectivity, and factory assumptions should be explicit.

topics.name: Quantum error decoding
topics.description: Decoders infer likely errors from noisy syndrome data. Accuracy must be evaluated together with throughput, latency, and robustness to model mismatch.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Quantum error correction and logical circuits
taxonomy.assessment: Logical error budgets, gate factories, connectivity, decoder latency, and runtime

taxonomy.name: Error mitigation and near term reliability
taxonomy.description: Error mitigation changes estimators or experiments to reduce bias without providing the full protection of a fault tolerant encoding. Sampling overhead and assumptions must be reported.

topics.name: Zero noise extrapolation
topics.description: Zero noise extrapolation fits results measured at increased noise to estimate a lower noise limit. Extrapolation introduces variance and model dependent bias.

topics.name: Probabilistic error cancellation
topics.description: Probabilistic cancellation represents an inverse noise process through weighted sampling. Reliable channel knowledge and sampling overhead limit applicability.

topics.name: Readout error mitigation
topics.description: Readout mitigation adjusts observed outcome statistics using a measurement error model. Correlated errors and calibration drift can invalidate simple assignment matrices.

topics.name: Symmetry verification and postselection
topics.description: Symmetry checks reject or reweight outcomes that violate a known constraint. Acceptance probability and postselection bias must be reported.

topics.name: Virtual distillation and purification
topics.description: Virtual distillation uses multiple copies or related estimators to suppress some mixed state errors. Coherent errors and measurement costs remain relevant.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Noise channels, statistical estimation, and circuit execution
taxonomy.assessment: Estimator bias, variance, model mismatch, calibration drift, and shot overhead

taxonomy.name: Characterization verification and benchmarks
taxonomy.description: Characterization measures device behavior; verification tests specified claims; benchmarking compares workloads. Each answers a different question and needs an appropriate uncertainty model.

topics.name: Quantum state and process tomography
topics.description: Tomography reconstructs a state or channel from informationally complete data. Reconstruction method, confidence, and physical constraints affect the estimate.

topics.name: Randomized benchmarking
topics.description: Randomized benchmarking estimates average error behavior through randomized sequences. Interpreting the fitted decay requires checking gate dependence and noise assumptions.

topics.name: Gate set tomography
topics.description: Gate set tomography jointly estimates operations and preparation and measurement errors. Gauge freedom means some fitted quantities are not uniquely identifiable.

topics.name: Classical shadows
topics.description: Classical shadows use randomized measurements to predict many observables. Sample requirements depend on the measurement ensemble and target observable family.

topics.name: Quantum volume and application benchmarks
topics.description: System benchmarks summarize performance on specified circuit or application families. Different metrics are complementary and do not supply a universal ranking.

topics.name: Verification and quantum certification
topics.description: Verification and certification test a precise state or computation claim under a trust model. Protocol guarantees need to be read together with device assumptions.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Quantum measurements, estimation, and statistics
taxonomy.assessment: Identifiability, confidence intervals, trust assumptions, and workload definition

taxonomy.name: Software programming and compilation
taxonomy.description: Quantum software translates a problem into executable circuits and measured results. Compiler decisions should preserve semantics while adapting operations to hardware constraints.

topics.name: Quantum programming languages
topics.description: Programming languages express quantum operations alongside classical computation. Control flow, type safety, and provider execution models determine practical capabilities.

topics.name: Quantum intermediate representations
topics.description: Intermediate representations support compilation and interchange across tools. Semantics and classical control must survive translation between representations.

topics.name: Quantum circuit synthesis
topics.description: Circuit synthesis decomposes target transformations into allowed operations. Approximation accuracy and target gate set determine circuit size.

topics.name: Qubit mapping and routing
topics.description: Placement and routing adapt logical circuits to hardware connectivity. Inserted operations change depth, noise exposure, and execution cost.

topics.name: Quantum compiler optimization
topics.description: Compiler optimizations simplify circuits or exploit device characteristics. Semantic correctness and the validity of a noise objective should be checked independently.

topics.name: Quantum software testing and formal methods
topics.description: Testing and formal methods address errors in quantum programs and compilation. Assertions, equivalence, and statistical testing have different guarantees.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Programming, compiler concepts, and circuit semantics
taxonomy.assessment: Semantic preservation, target constraints, verification, and reproducibility

taxonomy.name: Classical simulation and hybrid systems
taxonomy.description: Classical simulators support development, verification, and baselines. Their scalability depends on entanglement, circuit structure, precision, and memory bandwidth.

topics.name: State vector and density matrix simulation
topics.query: quantum state vector density matrix simulation
topics.description: State vector simulation tracks amplitudes, while density matrix simulation tracks mixed states. Memory grows exponentially and differs substantially between these representations.

topics.name: Tensor network simulation
topics.description: Tensor network methods exploit circuit structure and limited entanglement. Bond dimensions and contraction order control practical cost.

topics.name: Stabilizer circuit simulation
topics.description: Stabilizer simulation efficiently handles Clifford operations and suitable states. Non Clifford extensions require additional resources or approximation.

topics.name: Quantum GPU and HPC integration
topics.query: quantum GPU high performance computing simulation
topics.description: GPU and distributed HPC methods accelerate selected classical simulation operations. Memory bandwidth, communication, and precision determine real performance.

topics.name: Hybrid quantum classical workflows
topics.description: Hybrid workflows coordinate classical processing with quantum execution. Batching, data movement, scheduling, and asynchronous control affect end to end cost.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Numerical linear algebra, parallel computing, and circuit structure
taxonomy.assessment: Memory, entanglement, precision, communication, and comparison to hardware

taxonomy.name: Architecture cloud and distributed computing
taxonomy.description: Architecture combines qubits, classical control, compilation, and communication into a system. Distributed designs must include entanglement costs, synchronization, and failures.

topics.name: Quantum processor architecture
topics.description: Processor architecture combines connectivity, instruction execution, control, and packaging. The best design depends on the workload and error correction strategy.

topics.name: Distributed quantum computing
topics.description: Distributed computation uses entanglement or remote operations across processors. Partitioning and communication overhead must be included in scaling claims.

topics.name: Quantum cloud execution
topics.description: Cloud execution provides remote access and job orchestration for quantum devices. Queue delays, device changes, and preserved experiment metadata affect reproducibility.

topics.name: Quantum circuit cutting
topics.description: Circuit cutting reconstructs a larger circuit from smaller experiments and classical postprocessing. Sampling overhead can grow rapidly with the number and type of cuts.

topics.name: Quantum memory architecture
topics.description: Quantum memories preserve states for later operations or communication. Lifetime, retrieval efficiency, fidelity, and interface compatibility determine their role.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Quantum hardware, compilation, and distributed systems
taxonomy.assessment: Connectivity, scheduling, communication, queueing, and complete system cost

taxonomy.name: Quantum networks and communication
taxonomy.description: Quantum networking distributes quantum states or entanglement between nodes. Protocols and hardware must account for loss, timing, storage, and classical coordination.

topics.name: Quantum teleportation
topics.description: Teleportation transfers a state using shared entanglement, measurements, and classical messages. It does not transmit usable information faster than light.

topics.name: Quantum repeaters
topics.description: Repeaters extend entanglement distribution beyond direct transmission limits. Rates depend on memories, losses, purification or coding, and coordination.

topics.name: Entanglement distribution and routing
topics.description: Entanglement routing allocates links and swapping operations to network tasks. Probabilistic success and memory decoherence require different metrics from ordinary packet routing.

topics.name: Quantum internet protocols
topics.description: Quantum network protocols coordinate physical links, entanglement, and applications. Layer interfaces must represent limited and consumable quantum resources.

topics.name: Quantum communication capacity
topics.description: Channel capacities quantify asymptotic communication rates under specified assistance. Classical, quantum, and private capacities answer different coding questions.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Quantum channels, entanglement, and networking
taxonomy.assessment: Loss, memory lifetime, heralding, synchronization, and capacity assumptions

taxonomy.name: Quantum cryptography and security
taxonomy.description: Quantum cryptography uses quantum systems for security tasks, while post quantum cryptography uses classical algorithms designed to resist quantum attacks. Their mechanisms and deployment requirements are different.

topics.name: Quantum key distribution
topics.description: QKD establishes secret keys under a stated device and security model. Finite size analysis, authentication, and side channels are part of practical security.

topics.name: Device independent cryptography
topics.description: Device independent protocols infer security from observed nonlocal correlations. Loophole closure, randomness, and finite statistics are demanding requirements.

topics.name: Blind and delegated computing
topics.description: Blind computing hides some information about a delegated task, while verifiable protocols also test correctness. Client capability and server trust distinguish protocols.

topics.name: Quantum cryptanalysis
topics.description: Quantum cryptanalysis studies attacks on classical or quantum security systems. Algorithmic complexity and physical fault tolerant cost should both be considered.

topics.name: Post quantum cryptography interface
topics.description: Post quantum cryptography uses classical schemes intended to resist quantum attacks. It is included as a security interface to quantum computing, not as a quantum hardware protocol.

topics.name: Quantum random number generation
topics.description: Quantum random number generators estimate and extract entropy from measured quantum processes. Security depends on the source model and the amount of trusted hardware.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Cryptographic definitions, probability, and quantum algorithms
taxonomy.assessment: Threat model, composable security, finite size effects, and implementation attacks

taxonomy.name: Quantum sensing and metrology
taxonomy.description: Sensing is an adjacent quantum technology rather than a synonym for computation. It is included because control, estimation, and quantum resources connect it to computing research.

topics.name: Quantum parameter estimation
topics.description: Quantum estimation studies how states and measurements encode unknown parameters. Bounds do not automatically imply an experimentally achievable estimator.

topics.name: Quantum magnetometry
topics.description: Magnetometry estimates fields using spin or other quantum probes. Sensitivity must be quoted with bandwidth, integration time, and spatial resolution.

topics.name: Atomic clocks and interferometry
topics.description: Clocks and interferometers exploit controlled phase accumulation for precise measurement. Stability, systematic shifts, and entangled probe preparation set limits.

topics.name: Quantum imaging and illumination
topics.description: Quantum imaging and illumination use correlations for specified detection or imaging tasks. Advantages depend on the noise, receiver, and comparison model.

topics.name: Quantum sensing with error correction
topics.description: Error corrected sensing seeks to protect useful signal accumulation while rejecting noise. The signal and noise operators must satisfy relevant conditions.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Quantum mechanics, parameter estimation, and experimental physics
taxonomy.assessment: Sensitivity, bandwidth, noise, trust, and whether bounds are attainable

taxonomy.name: Specialized scientific applications
taxonomy.description: Scientific applications must specify the observable or decision task and account for preparation and readout. These categories organize exploratory work without claiming universal practical advantage.

topics.name: Quantum algorithms for high energy physics
topics.query: quantum computing high energy particle physics
topics.description: High energy applications include field simulation and selected analysis tasks. Physical observable, truncation, and classical verification define the computational problem.

topics.name: Quantum algorithms for nuclear physics
topics.description: Nuclear applications target states, reactions, and observables of interacting particles. Model spaces and controlled physical approximations accompany circuit errors.

topics.name: Quantum algorithms for numerical integration
topics.description: Integration algorithms often build on amplitude estimation. The input oracle and required precision determine whether a query benefit survives end to end accounting.

topics.name: Quantum algorithms for engineering
topics.description: Engineering applications connect quantum algorithms to discretized models and inverse tasks. Conditioning and output extraction can dominate the workflow.

topics.name: Quantum algorithms for biology and drug discovery
topics.description: Biological and drug discovery proposals often depend on quantum chemistry subproblems. Chemical accuracy and downstream biological validation should be assessed separately.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Relevant scientific model and quantum algorithm prerequisites
taxonomy.assessment: Observable definition, model error, preparation, readout, and domain validation

taxonomy.name: Education research practice and ecosystem
taxonomy.description: Research practice includes learning, reproducing results, documenting limitations, and judging evidence. Roadmaps and standards describe plans or interfaces rather than proof that a device meets them.

topics.name: Quantum computing education
topics.description: Education resources teach prerequisites, conceptual models, and executable experiments. Curriculum scope and assessment quality determine how to use them.

topics.name: Quantum computing surveys and roadmaps
topics.description: Surveys and roadmaps organize a fast moving field and identify bottlenecks. Roadmap milestones are plans rather than demonstrated capabilities.

topics.name: Quantum standards and interoperability
topics.description: Standards and interfaces support consistent terminology and tool interoperability. The applicable version and scope should be recorded when used.

topics.name: Quantum reproducibility and research methodology
topics.description: Reproducible research records environments, circuits, parameters, datasets, and uncertainty. Fair benchmarks also preserve strong classical baselines and complete cost accounting.

topics.name: Quantum economics and sustainability
topics.description: Economics and sustainability studies evaluate full system cost and energy use. Cooling, classical support, runtime, and utilization matter alongside quantum device operation.

taxonomy.prerequisites: Basic quantum computing and critical reading
taxonomy.assessment: Source quality, environment records, fair baselines, versioning, and full system cost

paths.name: Foundations to algorithms
paths.goal: Build the mathematical and algorithmic vocabulary needed to read quantum computing research.

steps.text: Review Hilbert spaces, tensor products, and unitary operators.
Work with states, density matrices, and partial traces.
Understand gates, circuits, and universal models.
Implement a small quantum Fourier transform.
Study phase estimation with explicit precision and overlap assumptions.
Compare oracle query cost with complete implementation cost.

paths.output: A tested notebook for small algorithms, with input assumptions and classical comparisons.

paths.name: Quantum machine learning and hybrid AI
paths.goal: Connect classical ML experience to defensible quantum learning experiments.

steps.text: Account for the cost of encoding the dataset.
Compare a quantum kernel with classical kernels on the same split.
Build a variational classifier with a reproducible training loop.
Measure gradients and investigate trainability.
Read generalization and sample complexity results.
Evaluate GPU simulation cost and memory before scaling experiments.

paths.output: A benchmark report with held out metrics, uncertainty, encoding cost, and strong classical baselines.

paths.name: Quantum chemistry and simulation
paths.goal: Follow a physical problem from model definition to algorithm and resource estimate.

steps.text: Choose the basis, active space, observable, and accuracy.
Map fermionic operators to qubits and use valid symmetries.
Run a small VQE study with reference energies.
Compare digital simulation methods and error budgets.
Study block encoding and qubitization access assumptions.
Translate the algorithm into logical and physical resources.

paths.output: A small molecule or lattice demonstration and a transparent resource estimate.

paths.name: Error correction to fault tolerant architecture
paths.goal: Connect code properties to a complete logical computing system.

steps.text: Construct stabilizer checks and logical operators.
Simulate syndrome extraction under an explicit noise model.
Measure decoder accuracy and latency.
Map logical operations through lattice surgery or another stated method.
Include non Clifford resources and factory scheduling.
Combine distance, hardware, and runtime assumptions in an estimate.

paths.output: Logical error scaling plots and an architecture aware cost model.

paths.name: Hardware and experimental reliability
paths.goal: Evaluate one hardware platform using control and characterization evidence.

steps.text: Select a platform and understand its physical qubit model.
Study control pulses and parameter constraints.
Review calibration and drift tracking.
Interpret benchmarking with its model assumptions.
Investigate leakage, crosstalk, and correlated errors.
Assess mitigation with sampling overhead and bias.

paths.output: A platform comparison that distinguishes device metrics from logical performance.

paths.name: Quantum software and GPU systems
paths.goal: Build an executable workflow and understand its full software stack.

steps.text: Learn one supported programming framework.
Inspect intermediate representation and classical control semantics.
Measure the effect of mapping and routing.
Estimate state vector and density matrix memory.
Benchmark CPU, GPU, and distributed simulation where available.
Add semantic and statistical checks to the workflow.

paths.output: A versioned project with circuit definitions, environment details, and performance measurements.

paths.name: Networking and security
paths.goal: Separate quantum networking protocols from classical post quantum security.

steps.text: Understand teleportation and the required classical communication.
Study repeaters and memory and loss constraints.
Analyze entanglement distribution and routing.
Read QKD security with finite size and device assumptions.
Compare delegation, blindness, and verifiability.
Study classical post quantum cryptography as a distinct deployment path.

paths.output: A protocol comparison with explicit trust models, costs, and deployment requirements.

paths.name: Sensing and scientific applications
paths.goal: Choose a scientific target and distinguish computational from sensing claims.

steps.text: Define an estimation task and attainable measurement strategy.
Read sensing performance with bandwidth and spatial resolution.
Identify a concrete scientific or engineering observable.
Evaluate numerical algorithm assumptions and conditioning.
Specify what can be verified with the available measurements.
Prepare a reproducible comparison with complete uncertainty reporting.

paths.output: An application study with a specified observable, validation plan, and practical cost accounting.

methods.heading: Scope and taxonomy
methods.text: This is a broad research and learning map, not a claim to enumerate every possible topic or every available resource. The hierarchy contains major categories, topics, and fine subcategories. Networking, sensing, and classical post quantum cryptography are explicitly included as adjacent areas. These areas should not be conflated with quantum computation.

methods.heading: Authentic source records
methods.text: Scholarly entries were retrieved from the Crossref REST API using publisher deposited metadata and identifiable DOIs. Official web entries were retrieved from first party institutions, software projects, or providers and required a successful HTTP response and an identifiable page title. Failed or unrelated sources were excluded. The catalog is a metadata based bibliography, not a full text systematic review or a ranking of research quality.

methods.heading: Subject assignments and finer tags
methods.text: Topic searches were screened using title wording and subject context. Ambiguous results received editorial corrections or exclusion. Multiple supported discovery paths are retained as related topics. Fine subcategory tags are conservative lexical assignments from titles. Topic level only means that no precise fine tag was established; the full vocabulary shown in the taxonomy is not automatically assigned to every resource.

methods.heading: Dates and publication types
methods.text: Years and publication types follow retrieved bibliographic metadata. Posted content is kept separate from journal articles because peer review cannot be inferred from a DOI. Books and book chapters are distinct resource types, and separate editions can be retained when their years differ. Undated official pages stay undated; the retrieval year is not substituted for a publication year. Conference names are shown only when the source supplies an event or a proceedings venue.

methods.heading: Deduplication and selection
methods.text: DOIs and canonical web URLs were deduplicated. Identical normalized titles with matching lead author and publication year were also merged, preferring a journal or conference record over posted content when a match was clear. The selection balances topic coverage and retains curated foundational material. The same stable Q identifiers and resource records are used in HTML, DOCX, Markdown, PDF, CSV, and JSON.

methods.heading: What the verification status means
methods.text: Registered DOI means that a corresponding bibliographic record was retrieved from Crossref. It does not mean that every DOI resolver or full text download was individually tested. Page retrieved means that the official web page and its title were successfully retrieved on the snapshot date. Links can redirect, change, require authentication, or lead to paywalled content after delivery. No publication year, author, venue, or review status was invented to fill missing fields.

methods.heading: Coverage and limitations
methods.text: Coverage is selective and varies by topic, especially standards, economics, and specialized engineering. Bibliographic identity is stronger evidence than an unverified reference string, but it is not a guarantee of scientific validity, peer review quality, or practical advantage. Metadata can contain publisher errors or incomplete fields. Papers were not systematically screened for retractions and corrections across all external databases. Use the source record and paper itself when a claim is important.

methods.heading: Offline use and exports
methods.text: The HTML is self contained and uses no external scripts or fonts. Search, topic browsing, sorting, saved resources, and exports operate locally. External resource links need internet access. Browser saved resources use local storage and are not sent to a server. Search supports words combined with AND and quoted phrases. Journal, conference, author, publisher, year, type, topic, and verification filters can be combined. Exports contain all filtered results, while printing prints the currently displayed page of cards.
